live_fusion_findings.finding: The prior 15:01 Trigger-6 fusion is architecture-stale for the Perception Fabric because F2 advanced from a0b7696... through the WP709-WP714 perception sequence and subsequent Trigger-4/6 repairs. It remains historical provenance only for this subproblem.

Current F2 already defines single-owner bounded capture brokers, browser/rendered/<target_id> plus browser/structural/<target_id> logical sources, monotonic temporal fusion with uncertainty, source-generation hardening, and a later local physical browser-hook acceptance boundary. CDP/DOM/AX is therefore an existing planned adapter seam, not a missing product subsystem.

Primary Chrome DevTools Protocol source supports a thin dual-channel browser adapter: Page screencast/screenshot mechanisms can supply rendered observations; DOMSnapshot can supply structural observations; Target attachment supplies a debugging-session identity. Repository duplicate search found no pre-existing F2 CDP/Playwright/DOMSnapshot/Screencast implementation lane before the canonical claim.

Target.SessionID and Page.screencastFrame.sessionId are different causal identities despite similar naming: the former is a string debugging-session ID and the latter an integer screencast frame number. F2 must keep them typed/named separately before these fields enter provenance or replay.

Page.startScreencast is experimental in tip-of-tree CDP and absent from the old stable 1.3 subset; browser/CDP version identity must therefore be bound at the adapter boundary rather than assuming a timeless protocol ABI.

Rendered and structural observations sharing target/session provenance are correlated candidates, not proof of simultaneity. Each retains its own F2 monotonic capture timestamp and existing temporal uncertainty/fusion rules.

Navigation, target replacement, detach/reconnect or other invalidating browser transitions must advance the F2 source generation/epoch before new browser observations can fuse with old ones. This reuses the current Perception Fabric hardening law rather than inventing a second reset mechanism.

The browser adapter remains an observation producer only. Existing per-source broker ownership, temporal fusion, canonical state and effect/completion authority remain unchanged. Existing capture-authstream research handles portal/PipeWire permission/revocation and is not duplicated by this delta.

affected_modules: F2 local physical browser capture adapter seam

architecture_delta.expected_benefit: Prevents causal provenance aliasing and stale cross-navigation fusion while keeping the already-planned browser capture path thin and compatible with the existing Perception Fabric.
architecture_delta.runtime_efficiency_implication: Prefer a thin protocol adapter over a full automation framework unless target-browser tests demonstrate the heavier dependency buys materially better compatibility/reconnect behavior at acceptable CPU/RSS/latency/complexity cost.

hypothesis: A thin, version-bound CDP adapter with explicit dual logical sources and typed session/frame/generation provenance can close the browser physical-capture seam without creating another authority or duplicating temporal/capture infrastructure.
counterhypotheses: Experimental screencast behavior may be unstable enough that sampled Page.captureScreenshot is the better rendered primitive.
DOMSnapshot may be too expensive at the desired cadence; DOM/AX or a thinner structural projection may dominate it.
A full browser automation framework may materially outperform a thin adapter on reconnect/version compatibility and justify its dependency weight.
Rendered/structural skew under fast navigation may be too large for meaningful pairwise fusion without a browser-side synchronization/barrier mechanism.
falsifier_and_acceptance_gates: E5/build gate: bind one exact target browser build and protocol identity.
Compare Page.startScreencast with bounded Page.captureScreenshot for cadence, CPU/RSS, latency, drop behavior and reconnect stability.
Measure DOMSnapshot/alternative structural capture cost and rendered-vs-structural skew.
Exercise navigation, target detach/replace and reconnect; prove source-generation fences prevent stale fusion.
Verify Target.SessionID and screencast frame ID remain distinct through broker/provenance/replay surfaces.
Trigger-4 local physical acceptance must observe real browser capture before any physical or whole-system credit.
